claims.text: Increasing the fraction of hard atomic motifs in NiCoCr increases the amplitude of local shear-fault-energy fluctuations.
Larger local shear-fault-energy fluctuations increase dislocation pinning and resistance to dislocation motion.
Stronger dislocation pinning increases the yield strength of NiCoCr.
Local shear-fault-energy fluctuations and pinning produce wavy, intermittent or jumpy dislocation motion.
Equiatomic NiCoCr has a relatively uniform shear-fault-energy distribution with lower-amplitude fluctuations.
Systematic adjustment of elemental concentrations can promote hard atomic motifs and thereby increase local shear-fault-energy fluctuations.
Chemically hard atomic motifs are associated with local fluctuations in shear-fault energy.
High-energy regions in the fluctuating energy landscape act as barriers that pin or detrap dislocation segments.
The tailored alloy should have higher yield strength than equiatomic NiCoCr under otherwise identical test conditions.
The tailored alloy should show greater dislocation-path waviness and more intermittent motion than the equiatomic baseline.
A controlled reduction in shear-fault-energy fluctuations should reduce alloy strength.
A controlled reduction in shear-fault-energy fluctuations should diminish dislocation waviness.
The equiatomic NiCoCr baseline has more uniform dislocation paths than the proposed tailored alloy.
The proposed mechanism should hold at room temperature over a range of strain rates.
Processing conditions can change local chemical ordering and the range of planar fault energies in NiCoCr.
New phases or substantial changes in global chemical order may cause deviations from the predicted relationship.
The comparison should keep testing, processing and thermal history fixed while varying composition to influence hard-motif formation.

contradictions.description: The boundary and uncertainty fields treat phase transformations as excluded confounders that prevent isolation of the proposed mechanism, whereas the falsification rule treats observation of such confounding transformations as falsification of the mechanism rather than as an invalid comparison.
